questions.question: Which defect family are the remaining waves for: vacuous checks, drift between measurement and use, or both?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22, AskUserQuestion): 'Both, re-cut by family'. Epic 569 names TWO defect families going forward. Family A = the check that cannot fail (vacuous; check:null satisfied by the word 'attested'; no re-run helps) -- what all 15 unlaunched member issues were filed against. Family B = evidence true when taken, false when relied on (fails correctly when pointed at live state; caught by re-running every time) -- five pinned instances from waves 1-2: (1) test_code_map_precommit_e2e.py green only while code under test was uncommitted; (2) Admiral's '3564 passed' baseline taken from a commit message over an already-red base 244665ee; (3) PR #657's MERGEABLE + reviewer APPROVE + '0 failed' all true about a tree that was not the merge result; (4) trip-guard ROLLOUT CAVEAT true at authoring, never re-checked; (5) stale heartbeat used as liveness though it only advances on engine verbs. Waves 3-4 to be RE-CUT BY FAMILY rather than running the filed 15 in issue order; accepted that some filed A-issues get deferred or deleted if B carries the live evidence. Human declined the stated counter-case (that B is merely operator error re-running already catches). Consequence: the epic body needs a material_changes entry naming both families, and the w2-to-w3 replan packet's unlaunched_dispositions must be authored family-first.

questions.question: Does family C -- the unverified instrument -- get named alongside A and B, or fold into one of them?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'Name it as a third family'. Epic 569 closes on a THREE-FAMILY model, ratifying a taxonomy the human's q1 answer had ruled on while believing there were only two. FAMILY A = the check that cannot fail (vacuous; no re-run helps). FAMILY B = evidence true when taken, false when relied on (fails correctly when re-pointed at live state). FAMILY C = the INSTRUMENT measures a different thing than the code does -- neither vacuous nor stale; it fails loudly and correctly, against the wrong quantity. WHY C CANNOT FOLD, which is the load-bearing argument and must survive into the successor epic: A's remedy is 'make the check able to fail' and #459's check fails constantly; B's remedy is 'bind evidence to the basis it was taken against' and #524's evidence was taken against the correct, current tree. Both remedies leave C untouched. Applying A's remedy to a C defect is the specific mis-repair this naming prevents. MEMBERS: #459 -- the mutation-floor kill detector's regex cannot match ANSI, so under FORCE_COLOR every killed mutation reports HARNESS ERROR; measured on this box at one commit with no code change between runs, FORCE_COLOR=3 gives 10 failed while FORCE_COLOR=0 NO_COLOR=1 gives 14 passed exit 0, and a genuinely surviving mutant would arrive as one more HARNESS ERROR among ten. #524 -- an evidence script produced the headline 'unused: 2428 (64.7%)' by re-conflating the exact categories the gate it was reporting on had just separated, so the gate's work was right and the gate's own summary was wrong. LIVE INSTANCES FROM THIS RUN, not just filed ones: the map-freshness measurement, and heartbeat-as-liveness (the heartbeat only advances on engine verbs, so silence never means death). CORROBORATION: the epic's own filed title already reads 'attestation that can fail -- evidence, review, INSTRUMENTS'. C is most likely what 'instruments' meant when the epic was filed; it was never separated out because the body described only A. SCOPE: per q9 the human did NOT add a family-C lane to wave 3, so C is knowingly deferred to the successor epic with zero wave-3 coverage. This decision governs how it is NAMED there, not whether it is built now, and the epic summary must state the deferral explicitly rather than leave it implicit.

questions.question: Is measurement-vs-use one finding or five coincidences?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'One defect, common remedy'. Family B is ONE defect and gets ONE mechanism: evidence carries the basis it was taken against (blob OID / revision / tree state), and relying on that evidence re-checks the basis. #381's own proposed fix is verbatim this shape ('a red-proof claim carries the blob OID of the file it ran against, and the reviewing gate compares that OID to the shipped file; divergence is not automatically a failure -- it means the proof is stale and must be re-run, which is a mechanical check rather than a judgement'). Wave 2's #556 declared-locator work is the foundation to build on. The seven filed B-bearing issues (#381 #390 #515 #358 #388 #376 #221) become INSTANCES of the common mechanism rather than seven separate builds -- this is the re-cut q1 authorised, expressed concretely. Human declined: per-instance fixes (cheaper but nothing prevents the eighth instance), doctrine-only (#221's verified-against tag with no engine change), and measure-first (defers a wave). NOTE the standing constraint this must respect: the human's opening directive was 'fixing holes, not adding machinery for machinery's sake' and 'move work off the agent's plate onto a guided checklist'. A basis-carrying mechanism only satisfies that if the basis is captured BY the engine at evidence time rather than typed by the agent -- an agent-typed basis field is #503's --authority again (present, unfalsifiable, makes the record look stronger while proving nothing new), a hazard #515's body explicitly warns about. That constraint is now load-bearing on the wave-3 design and must appear in the launch order.

questions.question: #558: does the invoker-signs review level get built, and is reviewer count derived rather than free?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22), after OVERRIDING the Interrogator's first recommendation mid-question: 'Close it; route the real hole to the merge gate'. The human's pushback, verbatim: 'that's true that it always bubbles up to me, but I'd prefer we be rigorous so there's less that has to get to me. arguably we already do this in almost all cases. the dispatcher typically has a solid trust but verify attitude. is there actually something here? I am starting to think not.' They were right and the Interrogator's recommendation (settle two cheap halves) was withdrawn. DISPOSITION: #558 CLOSES. Reasoning, each half measured rather than argued: (1) 'the chain terminates at a human' is a doctrine line that enforces nothing -- the exact defect family A, so filing it would have had the epic commit its own sin in its own closeout; it also codifies as a virtue the escalation volume the human wants REDUCED. (2) 'derive n from the condition kind' invents a constraint on a dial that does not exist -- n is 1 everywhere in the corpus and no mechanism sets it; machinery for machinery's sake, against the opening directive. (3) 'does the invoker sign' already happens behaviourally; dispatchers run trust-but-verify. KEPT: the executor/reviewer/invoker cut ('is the claim true' vs 'does the true claim mean we are done') as one line of prose -- free, no gate, no condition, no count. THE REAL HOLE, found by going looking for where trust-but-verify is written down and finding it is NOT: skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md:194 ships the sequence 'verify checks green -> merge -> verify main HEAD advanced -> close'. NOTHING in that sequence inspects the MERGE RESULT before merging, and 'Re-validate after any promotion' is post-hoc, i.e. after main is already red. Live instance, ADMIRAL_LOG:135: PR #645 read MERGEABLE, merged clean exit 0, carried an independent reviewer APPROVE with zero findings and a correct commander suite report -- and produced a RED main. The defect existed on NEITHER PARENT: branch green, main green, merge red. No reviewer at any level could catch it because the failing thing does not exist until the merge happens, so MORE REVIEWERS IS STRUCTURALLY THE WRONG INSTRUMENT -- which is the substantive refutation of #558's premise, not merely a cheaper alternative to it. This is family B in the merge lane: 'branch is green' is true when measured and false when relied on to mean 'main will be green'. It is mechanisable, it takes work OFF the agent's plate rather than adding a gate, and it routes to wave 3 under agenda item 6 (no automated defence against a PR that reds main) as a family-B instance. ACTION OWED AT CLOSEOUT: post the measurement to #558 and close it; that close falls inside the delegated 'clear to close issues' latitude class.

questions.question: Which refresh flow is doctrine — attach-then-continue, or attach-then-idle-for-relaunch?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'Measure before deciding'. The Interrogator's recommendation (split the primitive into two evidence types) was NOT taken -- correctly, because it would have built a mechanism before establishing that refreshes are load-bearing at all, which is the opening directive's exact prohibition. DISPOSITION: wave 3 runs with the invoker POLLING for the 'REFRESH REQUESTED:' line and ACTUALLY RELAUNCHING when it appears, then wave 3's output is compared against wave 2's over-band lanes. The doctrine conflict stays unresolved on purpose until there are two waves of evidence rather than one. VERIFIED FACTS behind this. (1) Nothing consumes a refresh-request: every reference in checklist_engine.py is either has_pending_refresh_request() (the existence predicate), attach() (which stores the payload and stamps lease_claimed_at at line ~3865), or a comment. Its only two effects are unlocking the start/reopen guard under HARD and printing 'REFRESH REQUESTED:' on current. THE RELAUNCH IS THE REFRESH. (2) The two documents are not a contradiction to be resolved by picking one -- they are TWO DIFFERENT TRIGGERS SHARING ONE PRIMITIVE, and the evidence item they write is byte-identical. Trip-fired mid-work (global-everyone.md reach-up) = attach, go idle, invoker relaunches fresh. Arrived over the HARD band on turn one having done no work (LAUNCH_ORDER.template.md:76) = attach, start, do the work. An invoker reading 'REFRESH REQUESTED:' CANNOT DISTINGUISH THE TWO, so simply polling for the line would not have been sufficient either. This is the sharper framing and it is why the split-the-primitive option existed. (3) checklist_engine.py:1709 ROLLOUT CAVEAT predicted the exact failure: 'do NOT enable/exercise the HARD band in production until #183's tier-skill wiring lands -- an agent hitting HARD writes a refresh-request with no invoker watching and can strand.' #183 is CLOSED (2026-07-19), so the caveat is formally discharged, but the hazard it names is about the INVOKER'S ATTENTION and that half was never wired. (4) WAVE-2 MEASUREMENT, which cuts AGAINST refreshes being load-bearing: 8 refresh-requests raised (w2-ledger 2, w2-reindex 2, w2-basis 4); every lane finished attempt=1 with total_rework=0; and the lane that raised the MOST (w2-basis, 4) produced the strongest artifact of the epic. Three lanes, three merges, all working over-band with no refresh ever delivered. One wave is not proof, but it is the only evidence in existence and it points away from the mechanism mattering. WAVE-3 INSTRUMENTATION OWED, and it must be designed so the comparison can actually come out either way -- per q2's family C, an instrument that cannot distinguish the two worlds certifies nothing: record per lane the refresh-request count, whether a relaunch was actually performed, attempt/total_rework, reviewer verdict and round count, and whether the Admiral's own verify-before-merge caught anything the lane missed. Without a pre-declared comparison the wave-3-vs-wave-2 read will be a post-hoc story.

questions.question: Wave-1's two blocking lints: ratify, or reverse to report-only?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'Ratify blocking'. RegistrationLint, VocabularyRule (tests/test_check_script_registration.py:151, :228) and GaugeRecordFieldTableReconciliation (tests/test_gauge_writer.py:1739) stand as BLOCKING pytest tests, live on main since wave 1 via PR #644. Verified at ratification time: 82 passed in 0.18s; 19 allowlist entries, each individually verified against the repo by the clean-room reviewer. Rationale accepted: a pytest test that does not fail is a test that does nothing -- report-only there IS family A -- and the human's own commit 244665ee had already ruled against the --report-only reflex the Admiral wrote into this epic's contract. The human did NOT take the offered contract-tightening variant (pre-clearing 'a check expressed as a pytest test is blocking by construction' as a delegated class), so the latitude contract's classification of 'promoting report-only to blocking' as SURFACED remains unchanged and this decision does not generalise -- a wave-3 lane that wants to ship a blocking check must still surface it. THE ADMIRAL ERROR STANDS LOGGED AND IS NOT ERASED BY THE RATIFICATION: the launch order widened a surfaced decision class by pre-ruling it and letting the commander decide, and the outcome being endorsed after the fact does not make the process correct. Recorded as an episode candidate at closeout, because 'the ruling was right and the authority was wrong' is exactly the shape that goes unrecorded when the outcome is good.

questions.question: The three inert CommanderSpineBasisFields tests: re-pin, delete, or accept as-is?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'Fix granularity + make drift fail, not skip'. TWO DEFECTS FIXED, ONE PATTERN GENERALISED. Defect 1, GRANULARITY: CommanderSpineBasisFields (tests/test_checklist_engine.py:8543) pins PINNED_HEAD='9d5aac6daa58a72fc6a665cb39879ee5705f7f71' via 'git rev-parse HEAD' on the whole repo, so ANY commit to ANY file anywhere makes it inert -- which is why it is already dead one wave later (measured: 3 skipped in 0.11s, HEAD now 34e80a9e3ca8275b572782f50a8148cb3b2777a3). Re-pin to the BLOB OID of skills/commander/templates/COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json, which is the thing it actually depends on. #381 specifies blob OID for exactly this reason. Defect 2, FAILURE MODE: on drift it calls self.skipTest(). A test that can only skip is family A -- it cannot fail -- so the guard against family B is itself a family-A defect. The human already ruled this shape 20 hours earlier in commit c5ac6662 ('drop the witness test that could only skip'), verbatim: 'a check that can only skip is not evidence any more than one that cannot fail is.' Change to FAIL on drift with a 'this proof is stale, re-run it' message. That completes #381's actual proposal, which the implementer reached only half of: 'Divergence is not automatically a failure -- it means the proof is stale and must be RE-RUN, which is a mechanical check rather than a judgement.' Skip means never re-run. GENERALISATION AUTHORISED: skip-on-drift (repaired to fail-on-drift) becomes wave 3's worked example of the family-B mechanism q3 committed to. SIGNIFICANCE BEYOND THE FIX: no launch order asked for this. A sonnet crew member, implementing a hand-authored basis field, independently refused to certify a HEAD it had not been verified against and wrote the refusal into the test with an explicit message. That is unprompted convergence on the family-B remedy, and it is the strongest available evidence that the mechanism is one agents reach for naturally rather than machinery imposed on them -- which is the standing test the human's opening directive set ('fixing holes, not adding machinery for machinery's sake'; 'move work off the agent's plate'). Wave 3 therefore GENERALISES AN EXISTING CASE rather than designing from a blank page. The human did NOT take the narrower 'fix these, do not generalise yet' option, so the pattern is cleared to spread. NOTE the tension wave 3 must resolve honestly: fail-on-drift means the test goes RED whenever the template legitimately changes, which is a real cost paid by whoever next edits COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json. The mechanism is only a net win if re-establishing the basis is CHEAP -- so wave 3 must ship the re-verify path alongside the guard, not just the guard. A fail-on-drift with an expensive manual re-pin is how a guard becomes something agents route around.

questions.question: `spine: null` on every crew dispatch, 7 for 7: fix, or accept the workaround?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'Clear the pair on spine=None'. FIX: in scripts/run_crew.py, _crew_door_env() must EXPLICITLY UNSET SPINE_FILE and SPINE_SESSION when spine is None, instead of leaving the dispatching process's ambient pair inherited. The child then has NO door rather than the PARENT's door, so it cannot drive a run it does not own. Bounded: one function plus a test asserting both variables are absent from the child env when spine=None. DOCTRINE THIS OVERTURNS, and it must be overturned deliberately rather than silently: the current behaviour is intentional and documented at run_crew.py:1333-1341, which frames inheritance as the SAFE fallback -- 'No spine means the inherited-environment route is genuinely untouched, both variables together, exactly as crew_env()'s own contract already promises' -- and crew_env()'s own docstring at ~1280 repeats it ('a caller with nothing to bind still leaves the inherited value untouched, exactly as before'). Those comments are correct that the PAIR stays consistent; they are wrong that consistency is the property that matters. A consistent pair pointing at the PARENT's spine is precisely the hazard. The fix therefore also requires editing both docstrings, or the next reader restores the old behaviour as a bug fix. EVIDENCE: all 7 cli-backend implementers and reviewers dispatched this wave hit it; all 7 self-corrected; each named it INDEPENDENTLY in its own Workflow Feedback -- i.e. one trap rediscovered from scratch seven times, which is tribal knowledge rather than a mechanism. No bad state resulted this wave. SEVERITY ARGUMENT ACCEPTED: this is the same defect class as the Admiral's own wave-1 dispatch error one tier down, and THAT one did cost -- w1-wiring shipped with no independent review at any gate and needed a dedicated clean-room reviewer pass to recover. A fresh crew without the tribal knowledge drives the parent's spine. The human did NOT choose the leave-it-and-write-an-episode option despite the zero measured cost, nor the Admiral-fix-now option, so this lands as WAVE-3 SCOPE dispatched to a lane, not as an Admiral hand-fix. NOTE FOR THE LAUNCH ORDER: this is dispatch plumbing, not a family A/B/C defect, and it is in wave 3 on the human's explicit call rather than by family. It is also self-referential -- the lane fixing crew-door binding will itself be dispatched through run_crew.py -- so the lane must verify the fix against a real dispatched child rather than only against a unit test of the env dict.

questions.question: Does 'evaluate the 65' still need running, given w2-basis already measured 19 of them?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'Skip the census; promote the 9-per-19'. NO separate evaluate-the-65 measurement mission runs. The scheduled work item recorded at ADMIRAL_LOG:191 is hereby DISCHARGED BY EXTRAPOLATION rather than executed, on the strength of w2-basis's N=3 independent convergence over all 19 check:null conditions in COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json. THE PARTITION, which is now the epic's operative model: bucket 1 = 8/19 can express NO locator at all (a judgement with no artifact behind it); bucket 2 = 9/19 locator expressible with NO NEW MECHANISM, a direct check-kind promotion already gives them everything; bucket 3 = 2/19 genuinely gain from the new basis field, because a real artifact exists but the claim being made (convergence quality, triage quality) is a judgement no mechanical check can make. THIS ALSO ANSWERS THE HUMAN'S OWN DEFERRED PROMOTION TRIGGER, which was 'readjudicate where the blocker wants to be after evaluating the 65' (ADMIRAL_LOG:185): the blocking line is NOT a line across all conditions -- it is this three-way partition, and it falls BETWEEN BUCKET 2 AND BUCKET 3. WHAT THIS KILLS: the backfill of the basis field across qualitative conditions. Rolling a new field out to ~65 conditions to genuinely help ~7 of them is machinery for machinery's sake by the numbers, against the opening directive. WHAT IT DOES NOT KILL, and the launch order must not let a lane collapse these: q3's family-B remedy binds EVIDENCE (red-proofs, suite runs, review results) to the basis it was taken against; the 65 are QUALITATIVE CONDITIONS. Different populations. 2/19 is a verdict on the backfill, not on the mechanism. WHAT IT OPENS, and this is now the highest-yield work identified in the whole interrogation: bucket 2 is ~9/19, extrapolating to roughly 31 of the 65 -- conditions that could become REAL CHECKS TODAY with no new mechanism at all. That is family A, it is the epic's actual filed thesis, and it costs nothing to build because the check kinds already exist. RISK THE HUMAN KNOWINGLY ACCEPTED by declining both the full census and the sample: the 19 all come from ONE template (COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json). The other ~46 live in ADMIRAL_SPINE, EXECUTE_PLAN, REVIEW_SURVEY and siblings and may partition differently. The extrapolation is therefore itself a family-B shape -- a measurement taken on one population and relied on for another -- and the wave-3 lane MUST record, per condition it promotes, whether that condition's template matched the predicted partition. If the promotion lane finds the other templates partitioning materially differently, that is a material exception and triggers a replan rather than being absorbed silently.

questions.question: Does the epic still close with wave 4's reviewer machinery, or has its shape changed enough to re-cut?
questions.resolution: HUMAN ANSWER (Tommy, 2026-08-22): 'Wave 3, then close on the measured shape'. EPIC 569 RUNS ONE MORE WAVE AND CLOSES. This SUPERSEDES the latitude-time ruling 'Keep in 569' that placed WP5's eight reviewer-machinery issues as wave 4 -- that ruling was made on the epic's FILED shape and does not survive its MEASURED shape, which is exactly the contract-refresh case the Admiral doctrine names. WAVE 3, FOUR LANES: (1) promote bucket-2 qualitative conditions to real check kinds, ~9/19 measured extrapolating to ~31 of 65, family A, no new mechanism, highest yield identified in the whole interrogation [q8b]; (2) evidence carries the basis it was taken against, with fail-on-drift generalised from the repaired CommanderSpineBasisFields, family B, spec'd verbatim by #381 [q3 + q7]; (3) verify the MERGE RESULT before merging -- the hole found by refuting #558, family B in the merge lane, agenda item 6 [q4]; (4) run_crew.py _crew_door_env clears SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION on spine=None, dispatch plumbing [q8]. WHY WP5 DISSOLVED: it was grouped by SUBJECT (reviewers) and q1 re-cut the epic by FAMILY. Its eight land as #375 A, #223 A, #358 B, #388 both, #376 both, #363 neither, #558 closing per q4, #259 already closed -- six unrelated issues that all happen to mention reviewers, not a work package. AT CLOSEOUT, FILE AGAINST THE THREE-FAMILY MODEL rather than re-filing the old grouping: family C entirely (#524, #459 -- the unverified instrument, which no wave-3 lane touches); the engine-change family-B issues (#390 supersede-a-disproven-clause, #515 journal result/finding payload); the residual family-A issues (#518 zero-collecting selectors, #382 aliased-import guard + one-element fixture); the doctrine item #221 (verified-against provenance tag); and the dissolved WP5 remainder. The human did NOT take the add-a-family-C-lane option, so family C is knowingly deferred to the successor epic with no wave-3 coverage -- that deferral is deliberate and must be stated in the epic summary rather than left implicit. TWO SMALL ITEMS ROUTED AT CLOSEOUT, human notified and not objecting: map_orient verify-frame rejecting decision:X under DEGRADED (agenda item 7, never examined this run), and #259's item 1 (the perturb-to-test data-loss hazard that fired for real on f1Brainz) which sits closed with no resolution recorded anywhere -- needs reopen or an explicit recorded disposition. WHAT 569 WILL HAVE DELIVERED: mechanism across three waves plus a corrected taxonomy, which is the more durable half. The epic was filed believing in one defect family; it closes having measured three, refuted its own #558 premise on evidence, and discharged its evaluate-the-65 trigger by extrapolation instead of by a mission.

signoff.by: Tommy (fredcai6) — the human at the keyboard, interactive mode
signoff.statement: Signed off 2026-08-22 via the finish-gate question, after answering all 10 decisions himself and overriding the Interrogator's stated recommendation twice (q4, where his mid-question pushback -- 'is there actually something here? I am starting to think not' -- refuted #558 and withdrew the recommendation; and q5, where he refused the split-the-primitive build in favour of measuring first). Confirms questioning is complete and the understanding is shared: three defect families named (A vacuous, B drift, C unverified instrument), wave 3 scoped to four lanes, epic 569 closing after it on the measured shape with the remainder re-filed against the three-family model. Cleared the Admiral to consolidate, release the lease, author the w2-to-w3 replan packet, and refresh the expired latitude contract before any wave-3 dispatch.
